n: Right after His baptism, the Spirit leads Jesus into the wilderness. The Joseph Smith Translation says He went “to be with God,” and the temptations came afterward.

f.w: led up of the Spirit into the wilderness
f.g: JST: “led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be with God.”

n: Jesus fasted forty days and nights and afterward was hungry. Moses and Elijah also fasted forty days; Israel wandered forty years. Jesus succeeds where Israel struggled.

f.g: Hungry. JST adds that He had been communing with God.

n: The tempter comes: “If you are the Son of God, turn these stones into bread.” Satan targets physical hunger and tries to make Jesus doubt the Father’s declaration at His baptism.

f.w: If thou be the Son of God

n: Jesus answers with scripture: people need more than bread — they live by every word from God. He uses God’s word as His defense.

f.w: Man shall not live by bread alone

n: Next, Jesus is taken to Jerusalem and stands on the high corner of the temple. JST says the Spirit set Him there, not the devil.

f.g: Jerusalem.
The highest point or wing of the temple complex, high above the Kidron Valley.
JST: “Jesus was in the holy city, and the Spirit setteth him on the pinnacle of the temple.”

n: Satan now quotes scripture himself: “Throw Yourself down — God promised angels would catch You.” Scripture can be twisted out of context to justify wrong.

f.w: He shall give his angels charge concerning thee

n: Jesus replies, “It is also written: Don’t put the Lord your God to the test.” Faith trusts God; it doesn’t demand that He prove Himself.

f.w: Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God

n: Finally Jesus is shown all the kingdoms of the world and their splendor from a very high mountain.

f.g: JST again says the Spirit, not the devil, took Him there.

f.w: all the kingdoms of the world

n: Satan offers it all — if Jesus will bow and worship him. The temptation is to gain power by a shortcut that bypasses the cross.
Jesus commands, “Get away, Satan!” and cites scripture: worship and serve God alone. Moses rebuked Satan in a similar way.

f.w: Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God

n: The devil leaves, and angels come and minister to Jesus. Resisting temptation brings heavenly help.

f.w: angels came and ministered unto him

n: When Jesus hears John has been imprisoned, He goes to Galilee to begin His public ministry there.
He moves from Nazareth to Capernaum, a fishing town on the Sea of Galilee in the old tribal lands of Zebulun and Naphtali. Capernaum became His ministry base.

f.g: A town on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee.
Zebulun and Naphtali, two of Israel’s tribes.

n: This fulfilled a prophecy of Isaiah.

f.g: Isaiah.

n: Isaiah named this region — Zebulun, Naphtali, Galilee of the Gentiles. It was the first area conquered by Assyria and later heavily mixed with Gentiles, yet it would see the Messiah first.
People sitting in darkness have seen a great light. Jesus is that light, dawning on those overshadowed by death.

f.w: The people which sat in darkness saw great light

f.g: Deep darkness.

n: From then on Jesus preached, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near” — the same message as John.

f.w: Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand

n: Walking along the Sea of Galilee, Jesus sees two brothers, Simon (Peter) and Andrew, casting nets — fishermen at work.

f.g: Peter (Greek Petros) means “rock”; Jesus gave him this name.
A freshwater lake about 13 miles (21 km) long, also called Gennesaret or Tiberias.

n: “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” Jesus turns their skills to a new purpose: gathering people to God.
They left their nets immediately and followed Him. Their quick response is a model of discipleship.

f.g: Immediately.

n: A little farther on, Jesus calls two more brothers, James and John, who were mending nets in a boat with their father Zebedee.

f.w: James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother

f.g: Repairing, preparing.

n: They also left at once — the boat and even their father — to follow Jesus. Discipleship can require leaving what is familiar.

f.w: left the ship and their father

n: Jesus traveled throughout Galilee, teaching in synagogues, preaching the good news of the kingdom, and healing every kind of disease. Teaching, preaching, and healing summarize His ministry.

f.g: Local Jewish meeting houses for scripture reading, prayer, and teaching.
Good news.

n: His fame spread throughout the Roman province of Syria. People brought the sick, suffering, demon-possessed, those with seizures, and paralyzed — and He healed them all.

f.g: Various.
Probably those suffering seizures (epilepsy).
Paralysis.

n: Huge crowds followed Him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan — from every direction.

f.g: “Ten Cities” — a league of mostly Gentile Greek cities east of the Sea of Galilee.
